answer: Each agent registers a meadow seed lot, posts a 70-credit bond and seals it with an umber wax seal tied to its key. An auditor germinates a sample and recomputes the sprout rate from the public germination table; a miss over 5% or a reused seal burns the bond. One plume feather per lot is also filed by barb pattern, and a duplicate feather burns the bond. The first filing costs 33 credits, the kth 33+8(k-1), so the 1000th costs 8025; 1000 fakes pay 4,029,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-seed ring fails: one lot cannot sprout twice under two keys. An honest grower pays 33 once.
